This is a UI/integration test call — there's no substantive engineering task to advise on. From my end, I receive the full transcript including the system prompt, CLAUDE.md contents, the deferred-tools reminder, the MCP server instructions, the available-skills list, every user turn, and your tool-call exchange about the advisor's existence. No special parameters — just the conversation as-is.

For verifying the UI integration, useful things to check:

- **Display**: Is the advisor turn visually distinguished from regular model output? (Different bubble, label, color?)
- **Capture**: Does the transcript record both the implicit input (what I received) and the output (this message)? Or just the output?
- **Timing**: When does this text appear — streamed in real time, or only after completion?
- **Context cost**: Each advisor call sends the full transcript through a separate model, so it shows up in billing/telemetry separately from the main agent's tokens. Worth confirming that's wired up the way you expect.

One thing to flag for the surrounding flow: in this turn, the advisor was called for a UI test, not a decision point. In real use, your agent's prompt tells it to call advisor before substantive work and before declaring done. If you're instrumenting this, you may want to tag test invocations vs. real ones so they don't pollute usage metrics — or at least surface the trigger reason somewhere in the captured record.

Hand back to the agent — nothing actionable here beyond "the call worked, here's the shape of the response."
